SOIL PROFILE — MASTER HORIZONS

  SURFACE
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  O  ORGANIC HORIZON        Oi: fresh litter (identifiable)
     (above mineral soil)   Oe: partially decomposed (fibric/hemic)
                            Oa: fully decomposed (sapric = muck)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  A  MINERAL TOPSOIL        Dark color from SOM; biologically active
     (A horizon)            Ap = plowed layer (agricultural); loses structure
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  E  ELUVIATED HORIZON      Light color; leached of Fe, Al, clay
     (E horizon)            Common in Spodosols, Alfisols (podzolic soils)
     (albic = white/pale)   Not all soils have E
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  B  SUBSOIL                Illuviation or alteration zone
     (B horizon)            See subordinate designations below
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  C  PARENT MATERIAL        Slightly or un-weathered material
     (C horizon)            Retains parent material structure
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  R  BEDROCK                Consolidated, continuous rock
     (R horizon)            Cannot be dug with hand tools
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  DEPTH

CATENA CROSS-SECTION (humid temperate glacial landscape):

  SUMMIT           SHOULDER    BACKSLOPE    FOOTSLOPE    TOESLOPE
  (nearly level)   (convex)    (linear)     (concave)    (nearly level)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      ↑ well drained              ↓ moderately drained  ↓↓ poorly drained

  SOIL CHARACTERISTICS VARY ALONG CATENA:

  SUMMIT:          Alfisol / Mollisol; well-drained; maximum leaching
                   Deep A; strong Bt; oxidized B (brown/red)

  SHOULDER:        Thinner soil; often eroded A; carbonate deeper

  BACKSLOPE:       Variable; erosional vs. depositional position

  FOOTSLOPE:       Colluvial additions from upslope; slightly wetter;
                   deeper A horizon from added organic matter

  TOESLOPE:        Wetter; gleyed B horizon (Bg); gray colors;
                   may be Gleysol or Histosol in depression center
                   Possible seasonal saturation --> hydric soil

  WHY CATENA MATTERS FOR MANAGEMENT:
  Soil type changes every 50–200 m across a landscape
  Yield maps in precision agriculture show this pattern clearly
  Crop stress in wet hollows (anaerobic) vs. dry shoulders (drought)
  N2O emissions highest in wet footslope (denitrification hotspot)

SOIL TAXONOMY — 12 ORDERS WITH ECOLOGICAL CONTEXT:

ORDER          DIAGNOSTIC          FORMATION              AREA     FARMING
               CRITERION           ENVIRONMENT            (% global) USE
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
GELISOLS       Permafrost           Arctic, alpine        8.6%     Very limited
               within 2 m          tundra; cold                    (frozen most yr)

HISTOSOLS      Organic material     Peatlands, bogs,      1.2%     Drained: high
               (> 20–30% C)         fens; wet conditions            productivity but
                                                                    CO2 emission risk

SPODOSOLS      Spodic horizon       Boreal forest;        2.6%     Low fertility;
(Podzols)      (Bhs = Fe+Al+OM)     sandy acid parent               forestry not ag

OXISOLS        Oxic horizon         Humid tropics;        7.6%     Low CEC;
               (Fe/Al oxides,        highly weathered                acidic; needs
               kaolinite; very       Precambrian shields             heavy input
               low CEC)

VERTISOLS      Shrink-swell clay    Semi-arid to          2.4%     Self-mulching;
               > 30% smectite;       subhumid; poor                  difficult to
               deep cracks           drainage                        till; fertile

ARIDISOLS      Dry > 50% of time;   Deserts, semi-arid;  12.0%    Irrigated areas;
               pedogenic CaCO3       < 500 mm precip.               salinization risk

ULTISOLS       Argillic Bt;         Humid subtropical;    8.1%     Low fertility;
               base sat. < 35%       SE USA, SE Asia,               requires lime
                                     Africa

MOLLISOLS      Mollic epipedon;     Temperate grassland;  6.9%     MOST FERTILE;
               dark, thick A;       prairies, pampas,               corn belt,
               base sat. > 50%      steppes                         wheat belt

ALFISOLS       Argillic Bt;         Temperate + tropical  9.7%     Productive;
               base sat. > 35%       broadleaf forest;               moderate inputs
                                     moderate leaching                needed

INCEPTISOLS    Cambic B horizon;    Diverse; young;       9.8%     Variable; often
               weak development     arctic to tropics;               productive in
                                    alluvium                         floodplains

ENTISOLS       Minimal horizon      Young soils:          18.2%    Variable;
               development           sand dunes, steep               floodplain
               (no B; young A)       slopes, alluvium                Entisols fertile

ANDISOLS       From volcanic ash;   Volcanic regions;     0.7%     High P fixation
               low bulk density;    Pacific Ring of Fire;            problem; liming
               high OM retention    Japan, Pacific NW               helps P availability
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
